t: Begun by educated Indians seeking reform, the Indian National Congress grew under Mahatma Gandhi into a mass movement whose non-violent campaigns drew millions into the struggle against British rule.
It was never one body: moderates, radicals, revolutionaries, the Muslim League, peasants, workers, opponents of caste and the people of the princely states pursued different, often conflicting aims.
British rule ended on 14–15 August 1947 with the partition of British India into India and Pakistan, which uprooted some fifteen million people and was accompanied by killings on a vast scale.
dyk: Gandhi took no part in the independence celebrations in Delhi: he spent 15 August 1947 in Calcutta, fasting, praying and spinning in a house in a riot-torn district that he shared with the Muslim League leader Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy.
ev: The Indian National Congress holds its first session in Bombay
Lord Curzon’s partition of Bengal provokes the Swadeshi movement and the boycott of British goods
Troops fire on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, killing hundreds
Gandhi leads the Non-cooperation movement, in alliance with the Khilafat movement
Gandhi’s Salt March to Dandi begins a nationwide campaign of civil disobedience
The Muslim League’s Lahore Resolution demands independent states for the Muslim-majority areas
The Congress launches the Quit India Movement, and its leaders are imprisoned
British rule ends, and British India is partitioned into India and Pakistan

f.where: British India and the princely states, from Bengal and the Punjab to Bombay, Madras and the North-West Frontier, with supporters among Indians in Britain, South Africa, North America and South-East Asia
f.period: 1885–1947: from the first session of the Indian National Congress in Bombay to the independence of India and Pakistan on 14–15 August 1947
f.figures: Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Subhas Chandra Bose, Muhammad Ali Jinnah
f.outcome: The end of British rule in 1947, with British India partitioned into the independent dominions of India and Pakistan amid mass migration and communal violence
